data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, Alagar is revered as a form of Lord Shiva, known for his protective and guardian qualities. He is the presiding deity of the ancient temples of Alagar Kovil in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. Alagar is also associated with Chola dynasty, as King Rajaraja Chola I perished protecting the temple during an invasion by Kolattar Segar.
data.spiritual_significance: Alagar is considered to be the embodiment of protection, courage, and strength. He represents the divine force that safeguards us from the inner and outer challenges of life. His name signifies faith, devotion, and the belief that the divine is always watching over and protecting us.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Alagar is a popular name for Lord Murugan in Tamil Nadu, India. The name Alagar carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Alagar is a form of Lord Murugan, a Hindu deity.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Alagar, a teacher in Delhi, India, shares that their name Alagar meaning "Protector of the World" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Alagar signifies the supreme self, the pure consciousness that transcends all dualities. It is the form of Lord Vishnu revered in Tamil Nadu, symbolizing liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
